status: Partially fixed in source pending governed publication
area: Long validator execution / framework quickfix commit authority
finding: Standard and full validator profiles could run longer than a task authority TTL without an automatic durable run id, batch progress, heartbeat, or status snapshot, so operators could not distinguish progress from a hang and a completed run could fail to become task evidence. During the bounded repair, both frozen and source-first git commit facades also rejected a live taskless framework claim as missing authority, leaving no executable source-only recovery while unrelated staged governance residue had to remain untouched.
expectedBehavior: Every long validator profile must automatically expose a durable run id, weighted progress, current batch, heartbeat, status query, and resume command while preserving pass/fail semantics. A live exact framework claim must be recognized consistently by dry-run and write commit paths, and a source-only candidate must not infer a linked task receipt or require modification of foreign staged bytes.
evidenceOrRepro: A full validation run exceeded the default authority window without a durable evidence update. Focused tests now prove automatic run creation, progress from 0 through 100 percent, batch identity, heartbeat output, final status retention, and resume metadata. The subsequent governed dry-run returned ATM_GIT_COMMIT_DRY_RUN_PURITY_VIOLATED even though framework-mode status showed the exact active lock; a path-bounded emergency commit was required after temporarily preserving and restoring the foreign staged deletion byte-for-byte.
followUp: Publish commit 81057db8b2696dcc9a7db2af6c61aa80e8fc5018, run the standard and full profiles through task evidence with observable progress, and repair taskless framework-claim resolution so future bounded source-only quickfixes can use the normal governed commit facade without emergency index handling. This follows INV-ATM-013 and INV-ATM-014.
